result.summary: PASS. Reviewed git diff main...HEAD (lib/letflow/engine.ex, lib/letflow/engine/execution_error.ex) against the four idiom questions: (1) Idiomatic vs crutch -- ExecutionError.append_multi/3 is a pure, composable Ecto.Multi appender (zero Repo calls of its own, INV-EE61-7), matching TaskActivation's existing composable shape exactly; complete_task/3's rewired Multi.merge/2 branch point (build_complete_task_tail_multi/6) is the same idiomatic mechanism the module already used pre-REQ-061 for its normal-path tail, extended to two branches rather than one -- no hand-rolled state machine, no case-on-atom masquerading as a state machine. (2) Supervision -- confirmed no process/supervision-tree changes in this diff (grep for InstanceSupervisor/gen_statem/GenServer shows only pre-existing references); this requirement is transactional DB/business logic only, isolation model untouched. (3) Type-safety -- error_type()'s open union (trailing atom()) and the {:merged,_}/{:execution_error,_} and {:advanced,_}/{:execution_error,_} tagged-tuple outcomes are a reasonable typed-union upgrade over the prior bare {:error,_}; no new representable-invalid-state gap introduced worth a docs/issues/ filing. (4) Scope creep -- none found; set_instance_error/2 and ExecutionError.append_multi/3 build exactly the design doc's two entry-point shapes and no more, with REQ-056/057/062 left as named future callers rather than stubbed early. No docs/anti-patterns.md entry applies. TWO FLAGGED ITEMS, both signed off: (A) AC4 interim reading ACCEPTED -- REQ-061's own depends_on: [REQ-048, REQ-050] (not REQ-056/057/062) confirms this requirement was never sequenced to require those three to exist first; they are listed 'pending' with zero shipped code in stage-3-instance-engine.md, verified independently by REVIEWER, not taken on the design doc's word. REQ-061 is explicitly the shared-sink infrastructure other requirements build call sites against, so blocking it on callers that don't exist yet would invert the intended build order. '2 of 2 currently-shippable callers wired, 3 named as future call sites with open questions recorded' is accepted as satisfying AC4's intent for this run; flagging for RELEASE-VALIDATOR/ORCH that AC4's literal 'at least three' wording should be mechanically re-verified once REQ-056/057/062 each land (non-blocking follow-up, not a condition of this PASS). (B) Arity-widening deviation ACCEPTED as safe and reasoned, not a problem -- the design doc's own §5.1/§5.2 prose (not just its @spec line) already specifies error_args() needs instance_id from the M2-locked InstanceProjection plus the caller's actor_id/idempotency_key 'threaded through', which a literal 2-arg pure function cannot access; the design's own @spec text (using a different name, merge_outcome_for/2, than the actual function) was itself the inconsistent artifact, not the implementation. ELIXIR-DEV's fix -- extra explicit parameters rather than a closure or process dictionary -- is the idiomatic Elixir choice, keeps the functions pure and testable, and was explicitly flagged rather than silently diverged. Non-blocking note: consider updating the design doc's §5.1/§5.2 @spec blocks in a follow-up doc pass so future readers aren't misled by the stale 2-arg signature, but this does not block PASS since the deviation is well-reasoned and disclosed.
